newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Arrest sought for S.Korean Hanbo founder - radio.
newsitem.headline: Arrest sought for S.Korean Hanbo founder - radio.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors will seek a warrant to arrest founder Chung Tae-soo of the troubled Hanbo Group on fraud charges, state radio said on Friday.
The prosecutors summoned Chung from a Seoul hostpital on Thursday and has since questioned him over a loan scandal involving the conglomerate's steelmaking flagship.
The Korea Broadcasting System said the prosecutors planned to ask a Seoul court to issue the warrant later on Friday. A prosecution spokesman said he could not confirm the report.

Hanbo Steel Co, South Korea's second largest steelmaker, defaulted on debt repayments last week after piling up about five trillion won ($5.8 billion) in loans from 61 banks and financial institutions.
State prosecutors said they questioned Chung and officials of creditor banks on how billions of dollars were funnelled to the financially shaky Hanbo Steel.
Chung had been admitted to hospital after complaining of high blood pressure on Tuesday but doctors said his health was relatively sound.
